display_name: Paul Hobbs Richard Dinner Cuvee Agustina Chardonnay, Sonoma Mountain
raw_content:
{
  "hook": "From vineyards high on Sonoma Mountain, the Richard Dinner Cuvée Agustina Chardonnay is shaped by rocky volcanic and clay-loam soils and long daytime sun above the fog line, producing a Chardonnay with concentrated stone-fruit density and a mineral backbone. Paul Hobbs frames that site intensity with measured oak influence and texture to keep the wine focused rather than overtly tropical.",
  "wine_summary": "Paul Hobbs's Richard Dinner Cuvée Agustina Chardonnay matters because it pairs a clear Sonoma Mountain site signature—elevation, volcanic-derived soils, and strong diurnal swing—with the winemaker's precision. Sonoma Mountain’s elevation (400–2,295 ft) and position above the morning fog push grapes to ripen with retained acidity and concentrated flavors; that combination is why the wine reads as citrus and white-fleshed stone fruit with saline/mineral notes rather than jammy California tropical fruit. The cuvée has performed well on the competition circuit (multiple TEXSOM medals across vintages), which reflects consistent execution vintage to vintage.",
  "terroir_expression": "Elevated sites on the eastern slopes of Sonoma Mountain sit above the fog line and on volcanic and rocky loam over clay loam; those soils drain quickly and stress the vines, producing smaller berries with higher skin-to-juice ratio and concentrated flavors. Longer daytime sun exposure increases ripe stone-fruit notes, while large diurnal temperature shifts preserve malic acidity, translating in the glass to taut acidity, saline minerality, and a compact midpalate rather than overt tropical ripeness.",
  "vinification_summary": "Paul Hobbs typically balances barrel fermentation and aging in French oak with neutral vessels and controlled malolactic conversion to achieve texture without blunting acidity; lees contact and occasional bâtonnage (stirring the lees) add creaminess and midpalate weight. Specific barrel percentages and malolactic rates for each vintage of this cuvée are not always published, but the house approach emphasizes structural clarity and restraint with oak as support rather than the dominant flavor.",
  "food_pairing": "Wood-grilled salmon with lemon and capers — acid and citrus cut the oak-driven richness while the smoky grill echoes the wine’s mineral notes; Roast chicken with herb butter (thyme, tarragon) — the wine’s acidity lifts the butter and the mountain concentration stands up to savory herbs; Seared scallops with brown butter, hazelnuts, and a squeeze of lemon — the nutty brown-butter flavors mirror subtle barrel spice and the acidity refreshes the palate; Dungeness crab with a light beurre blanc — the wine’s saline minerality and steady acid are a textbook match for sweet crab and a creamy sauce.",
  "comparable_wines": "Merry Edwards Dutton Ranch Chardonnay — similar Sonoma mountain/climate sourcing and a comparable balance of oak and citrus-driven fruit; Ramey Sonoma County Chardonnay — comparable focus on acid structure and measured oak, offering a like-for-like tasting experience for shoppers comparing premium Sonoma Chardonnays.",
  "style_profile": "Full-bodied dry white with bright acidity and toasty oak-driven texture",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Drink 2024–2032. Store at classic cellar conditions (50–55°F, stable humidity); enjoy earlier for primary fruit or mid-term for integration of oak and secondary notes.",
  "value_assessment": "Price: $60–85. Competitors in this range include Merry Edwards Chardonnay ($60–85) and Ramey Chardonnay ($50–75). It is worth the price for buyers who prioritize site-driven concentration and disciplined oak; you’re paying for Sonoma Mountain provenance and a producer known for consistent winemaking rather than anonymous bulk Chardonnay.",
  "market_position": "Sommeliers and boutique retail buyers list this wine where site-specific Chardonnay is valued—higher-end American restaurants, specialty wine shops, and direct-to-consumer mailing lists. Collectors who follow Paul Hobbs and consumers seeking a serious Sonoma Chardonnay are the primary audience.",
  "insider_take": "Compared with the butter-forward, high-alcohol California Chardonnays many shoppers expect, this cuvée offers more mineral lift and structural focus; buy it if you prefer acidity and depth over opulence. Skip it if you want overt tropical fruit and plush sweetness—the tradeoff here is precision and terroir expression instead of fruit-forward immediacy.",
  "aging_potential_years": 8,
  "drinking_window_min_years": 2,
  "drinking_window_max_years": 8,

    "aroma_intensity": "pronounced",

  }
}
